name: triplicity

attributes.attribute: held mystic importance by the Celts

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Triplicity is the state of being threefold. It is a cross-reference in Celtic myth to the number three, which the Celts held in mystic importance. The concept appears together with tripling in tales, as in the pattern of a triple goddess or a threefold death. To review this idea, see the entry for Three.

okr.objective: Define triplicity as a cross-reference to the number three.
